needsBespoke.why: Qiyana's damage is gated by a three-way mutually-exclusive Element state (Brush/River/Terrain) held via Terrashape (W), which determines Q's bonus effect (stealth+MS / root+slow / execute-style bonus damage), and resets Q's cooldown when refreshed. The fight description says fights have no terrain, but Qiyana spawns holding the Terrain element by default and re-gathering any element normally requires nearby brush/river/terrain geometry the arena would lack. This produces a state machine (one guaranteed 'free' enchanted Q at the start, then permanently vanilla Q afterward, and an R that structurally cannot deal damage without terrain to trigger its shockwave) that the closed primitive list can express piecewise but not as a single primitive; it needs bespoke sequencing/gating logic to decide what Elemental Wrath's bonus and R's shockwave actually resolve to in a terrain-less dummy fight.

unsettled.question: After Qiyana consumes her starting Terrain element on the first Elemental Wrath cast, can she ever regather an Element (and thus recast Elemental Wrath / benefit from W's on-hit magic damage, attack speed, and Q cooldown reset) again during the fight, given the arena has no brush/river/terrain?
options: No further Elements are ever available; all subsequent Q casts are the unenchanted Edge of Ixtal and W's passive/active never re-trigger after the first Element is spent
The simulator should assume some terrain/brush/river feature is always reachable so Qiyana can keep regathering Elements throughout the fight
quotes: Once ''Terrashape'' has been learned, '''Qiyana''' is automatically given the {{cci|Terrashape Rock.png}} {{sbc|{{as|Terrain}}}} element upon [[Death|respawning]].
''A target Element is required to cast this ability''.

proposal: Assume Qiyana begins the fight holding the default post-respawn Terrain (Rock) Element.

Open by casting Elemental Wrath (Q) to consume the Rock element, dealing its base physical hit (plus the 60% Terrain bonus only if the target is already below 50% max health, otherwise just the base Elemental Wrath value).
Cast Audacity (E) on cooldown throughout the fight for its flat+0.5 bonus AD physical hit; it also forces an immediate basic attack on arrival, which benefits from any active on-hit riders.

Weave basic attacks between ability casts whenever off cooldown/off cast-time, since attacks carry Royal Privilege's proc (subject to its per-target internal cooldown) and, while an Element is held, W's bonus on-hit magic damage and attack speed.

Recast Edge of Ixtal (Q) on cooldown for its base physical line damage; after the starting Rock element is spent and cannot be regathered (no terrain in the arena), treat all further Q casts as the unenchanted, non-Terrain version.

Cast Supreme Display of Talent (R) once available on cooldown as a formality, but its expected damage contribution is 0 in a terrain-less arena since its shockwave (the only damage-dealing part) cannot trigger without River/Brush/Terrain geometry.
Do not spend a cast on Terrashape (W) purely as an active beyond the implicit starting Element, since there is no terrain/brush/river to gather from and the active itself deals no damage.
Repeat E and Q on cooldown with attacks filling the gaps for the remainder of the ~15 s window.
questions: Should the simulator assume the arena contains at least one reachable terrain/brush/river feature so that W's active, R's shockwave, and repeated Elemental Wrath casts remain usable, or should Qiyana's kit be modeled strictly as 'one free Element at the start, nothing more'?
If R is expected to deal zero damage under the strict no-terrain reading, should it be omitted from the rotation and cooldown entirely rather than cast on cooldown for no effect?
Is the correct Royal Privilege ICD 14s or 25s, since that changes whether it procs once or twice inside a 15 s fight?

Since the target is a single stationary dummy, does Royal Privilege's per-target ICD get reset by Terrashape's 'gathering an Element with a different buzzword' clause if only one Element (starting Rock) is ever held, or is that reset clause simply inapplicable here?
